top3_gaps.gap: Crossing Hall portal arches are not shown at all: arch cameras frame a blank exterior plaster wall, fill the frame with a stone or wood surface, or look through a wooden arch into a black void. The eight arches, their biome signs and locked/open/sealed states cannot be read. The nave is a bare cobbled corridor with doors and lanterns, not a portal hall.

Open Meadows bands are broad uniform grass fields with thin repeated flower scatter and few groves, rocks or landform breaks. Distance is a low flat mountain strip with no mid-ground mass and no 15-80 m subject in many views, far from the key art's layered hills, groves and village-and-landmark composition.

Landmark and settlement set pieces read as blocky kit geometry. The Burrow hillside is faceted with flat rectangular dark patches and a flat brown ramp. The stronghold is a tiny far silhouette behind pylons, and its courtyard is a dark flat plain framed by banners. The relay yard floor carries flat hexagonal decals.

rows.reason: On approach the stronghold is still a tiny dark speck on the horizon behind a line of pylons, with no 400 m silhouette. Close up, the courtyard is now enclosed by stone walls with large oxblood Tether banners, braziers, machinery and crates, so it reads as an occupied place. The floor is still a broad, flat, dark, empty plain, and daytime frames are murky.

Inside the yard the ground is bare packed earth with no flowers growing through it, so the catalogued defect is gone. The yard now shows flat yellow-green hexagonal decal patches, an abrupt yard/meadow edge and a giant stone pier filling half the gameplay frame. It reads as unfinished, not as a trafficked work yard.

Hard isolated facets and dark slashes are largely gone. Band 1 shows a soft snow peak with continuous slopes. Elsewhere the backdrop is a low, uniform, hazy band of identical peaks hugging the horizon, which reads as a flat card with no foothill layering and no landmark mass.

Some variety is new: red-brown tall grass clumps, yellow flecks and a few rock clusters. Broad slopes are still an even green carpet sprinkled with the same pale white/lilac flowers, without clustered drifts, shrub mid-layer or rock breaks. The ground texture shows streaky blur.

The mill water is only glimpsed as a flat blue strip behind a grassy mound, so its banks cannot be fully judged, though the visible edge is still abrupt. The village road has coherent timber houses, a well, warm night windows and the farm with fence and scarecrow. Visible activity is one or two NPCs and no clustered life.

The Warrens hillside is still a set of flat planar faces with straight edges and large rectangular dark blotches. A flat brown ramp runs to a dark cut entrance, and an opaque white column stands beside it. It does not read as a natural earthen hillside.
